title: Midnight Bridge / Quietwave: Protocol and Telemetry Sampler
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic playlet for small-to-medium staged rollouts that start in the late evening (US PDT/EDT) — what we call a "Midnight Bridge". It combines a micro-rollout cadence, operator handoff templates for small night crews, and a telemetry sampler checklist designed to catch latency regressions and error-mode drift quickly without noisy false positives.

High-level summary (one-liner):
- Goal: ship the v1.12 inference routing patch with minimal user impact, detect regressions in the first 90 minutes, and have a clear, low-friction rollback ladder.
- Scope: hosted API + dedicated routing plane; no DB migrations; config-only feature flags.

When to use this playlet:
- Small traffic shifts (~1-10% initial traffic), low-risk config changes, or kernel swaps where the biggest risk is tail latency noise.
- Night launches where core daytime teams are out and the on-call/night crew must execute fast.

Quick rollout calendar (compact):
- T-minus 72h: announce to #release-ops + fill the watchlist doc. (owner: Maya)
- T-minus 24h: canary targets defined, smoke test script ready, runbook locked. (owner: Diego)
- T-minus 2h: deploy canary to 1 region, 1% traffic, monitor 15m windows. (owner: night lead)
- Launch window (T+0): after 30m stable, ramp to 5% (T+30). After 60m stable, ramp to 20% and schedule morning handoff (T+60). If any yellow/red signals at any step, pause and evaluate.
- T+90-120m: morning handoff doc posted in #release-ops and to Confluence; daytime engineers take over.

Operator roster + roles for night window:
- Night Lead (primary contact): triage comms, escalate.
- Traffic Shepherd: controls percentage ramp, executes toggles & config flips.
- Telemetry Scout: monitors dashboards and signal sampler.
- Rollback Steward: pre-approved to trigger rollback and execute rollback runbook.

Preflight checklist (must pass before T-minus 2h):
- [ ] Smoke test harness green locally and in staging (smoke id: smoke/ms-122).
- [ ] Canary image/config baked and pinned (SHA noted in release brief).
- [ ] All dependent services have health-check pass and recent deploy <=48h.
- [ ] Observability tiles pre-configured: L7 latency p50/p95/p99, request error rate, L4 infra errors, CPU/GPU throttling, KV cache hit rate.
- [ ] Chat channel #release-ops created + pinned message with on-call roster and phone numbers.
- [ ] Rollback artifact validated (previous stable config diff available, rollback runbook sanity-checked).
- [ ] Pager escalation tree verified (SRE, runtime, infra, product owner).

Night shift handoff template (what the morning team receives):
- Short summary: what was changed (one sentence).
- Traffic timeline: timestamps and percentage ramps taken.
- Key signals and snapshots: attach 5m and 1h snapshots of latency and error metrics.
- Known issues and mitigations in-place (e.g., tuned throttle, temporary feature-flag).
- Next steps and recommended watch items.

Telemetry sampler: focused lightweight checks to run during ramping (repeat cadence: 5m, 15m, 30m)
- Core request-level signals (by route): success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tail CPU/GPU utilization spikes.
- Token-level regressions: median tokens/sec and median token cost (approx) for the canary pool.
- Error shape: ratio of infra (503/502) vs application (500/4xx) errors; watch for error type shift.
- Queueing/backpressure: request queue length and average queue latency - if queue > N (see thresholds below) abort ramp.
- Cache/kv signals: prefix cache hit-rate drop >10% over baseline triggers investigation.
- External dependencies: auth token failure rate, upstream model serving 4xx/5xx counts.

Signal thresholds (starter):
- Immediate abort (red): p95 latency > baseline p95 * 2 for 3 consecutive samplings OR success-rate drop > 1% absolute and trending.
- Pause & investigate (yellow): p95 latency +30% over baseline OR small increase in infra 5xxs (absolute +0.5% over baseline) for two samples.
- Green: p95 within +/-10% of baseline and success rate stable.

Rollback decision tree (concise):
1) Critical failure observed (red threshold): trigger immediate rollback (Rollback Steward) -> scale down canary -> revert routing config -> confirm stabilization -> postmortem follow-up.
2) Yellow: pause ramp, collect detailed traces, re-run smoke tests against canary pool. If no resolution in 30m, escalate to daytime owners and hold traffic at current level.
3) Ambiguous noisy signal (spikes + partial recovery): hold for 60m with extra sampling, increase sampling granularity (1m tiles for 10m), if oscillation persists rollback.

Operational run commands (handy snippets for Traffic Shepherd):
- ramp set --pool canary --pct 1 -> 5 -> 20 (document each step with why and who approved).
- snapshot metrics --window 15m --save canary-YYYYMMDD-HHMM (attach to handoff).
- revert-route --to stable-2026-08-20 --confirm (Rollback Steward only).

Release notes draft (shortform to share in morning):
Title: v1.12 routing patch (Midnight Bridge staged rollout)
Summary: small routing and kernel selection fix that improves throughput for short-sequence requests; staged rollout initiated by Release Eng on 2026-09-01 02:00 PDT.
What changed: config tweak in adaptive router to bias CPU fallback for short sequences; small kernel swap in quantized path.
Observed during rollout: stable at 1% -> 5% with p95 within baseline; minor p99 blips observed at T+22m (see telemetry snapshot). No customer-facing errors identified.
Known issues: transient p99 spike in region-us-west-2; ongoing investigation.
Action items for morning: triage traces for p99 spike, confirm no billing/usage anomalies, run extended soak in canary pool for 4h.

Post-release quick retro prompts (to capture while fresh):
- What went well?
- What was surprising?
- Were our signal thresholds appropriate? Too noisy?
- Did the handoff template reduce friction?
- Immediate follow-ups (owners + ETA).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Should we add token-level cost telemetry to the real-time sampler (Priya to prototype)?
- Tighten the queue-length thresholds for GPU-backed pools (SRE input needed).
- Add an automated escalation to on-call PagerDuty if abort condition triggers (Liam to file ticket ENG-3499).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the sampling lightweight: we don't want the night crew staring at 50 charts. Focus on 5 high-signal tiles + quick trace link.
- If rolling at night repeatedly, consider setting a temporary longer quiet window (02:00-06:00) for high-risk kernels.

Appendix (quick references):
- Smoke run command: ./tools/smoke-run --id smoke/ms-122 --env staging
- Quick trace link pattern: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces?run={snapshot-id}
- Emergency rollback checklist link: Confluence: release-playbooks/emergency-rollback

----
If you take anything from this doc: pin the 3 sampler tiles early, and make the rollback steps a one-click action for the Steward. Save the verbose traces for the handoff, not for the first 15 minutes.

-- Maya
